answer: Checkpoint-anchored age resists sybils: an identity's tenure is measured against signed, externally-anchored checkpoints, so its claimed age cannot be back-dated or fabricated after the fact. A swarm created today cannot thread its way into looking old — no trellis of forged timestamps survives, because the dune of history is pinned to immutable anchors. Privileges that require real elapsed age across anchored checkpoints force an attacker to have committed identities long ago, which a reactive sybil flood cannot do.
